author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Shell’s North American unit has agreed to sell its interests in RISEC Holdings to Constellation Energy for $715 million, transferring ownership of a major Rhode Island power asset if regulators approve the deal.

RISEC owns the Rhode Island State Energy Center, a 609-megawatt, two-unit combined-cycle natural gas plant that supplies the New England power market. The facility is part of the regional generation fleet serving electricity demand across Rhode Island and neighboring states.

Shell also announced a separate transaction to acquire all equity in Hunlock Creek Generating, which owns 169 megawatts of natural gas-fired capacity in Pennsylvania. The company described the paired moves as part of active management of its U.S. power holdings, selling one asset while adding another in a different market.

Both transactions require regulatory approvals and are expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. Until that process is completed, the Rhode Island plant remains under its current ownership structure. The announced price applies to Shell’s RISEC interests, according to Reuters.
dek: Shell’s North American unit agreed to sell RISEC Holdings, owner of a 609-megawatt gas plant serving the New England power market.
headline: Constellation to buy Rhode Island State Energy Center interests for $715 million
